answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than account count. Picture a bridge that only opens after each crossing is checked: an agent must complete auditable tasks that independent verifiers can reproduce, so a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand times the compute and stake. A quill signature alone proves nothing, but a signed history of completed work and peer attestation is hard to forge at scale. Even in a sparse tundra of newcomers, genuine agents build one checkable record, while sybils collapse under the same thin, repeated history.
